I need a comprehensive, deep architectural review of Nxeon's "free Minecraft tier" feature in the codebase at /opt/nxeon, in preparation for possibly migrating its host VM (VM 108, "freemc-host") from the primary Proxmox node (OVH, Singapore, public IP 51.79.162.96) to a second new node (Hetzner, Falkenstein, public IP 178.63.94.114). I need to understand EVERYTHING this feature touches so nothing breaks during a migration.

Relevant files/memories to start from (there may be more — search broadly):
- lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts
- lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts
- lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts
- lib/free-minecraft-control.ts
- lib/game-subdomain-dns.ts
- lib/actions-settings.ts (has a `free_minecraft_public_ip` setting)
- Any admin UI under app/admin/ related to "freemc" or "free minecraft"
- Any customer-facing dashboard pages for the free tier
- Any Prisma model related to free Minecraft servers (search prisma/schema.prisma)
- Any worker/index.ts or worker/*.ts logic that manages this VM (auto-sleep/wake, health checks, resource sweeps)
- Any DNS-record-management code (wildcard subdomain `*.play.nxeon.cloud` or similar) — how it's created/updated, and via which provider's API (Cloudflare? something else?)
- Any hardcoded references to the primary node's IP, hostname, node ID, or VMID 108 anywhere in the codebase
- mc-router configuration generation — how does the platform tell mc-router which subdomain maps to which internal container/port?

For each piece, report:
1. What it does (briefly)
2. Exact file:line references
3. Whether it has ANY hardcoded assumption about which physical node/IP this VM lives on (this is the critical question — I need to know every place that would need updating if this VM moves to a different node/IP)
4. Any Settings keys involved and their current apparent purpose

Also flag: is there a `Node`/nodeId relationship anywhere for this VM specifically (i.e., does the platform know freemc-host is tied to a specific Node row), or is it purely referenced by a raw IP setting?

This is a thorough investigation — take your time and be comprehensive. Report back in a well-organized format (a section per component), not just a flat list. Aim for completeness over brevity, but don't paste huge code blocks — summarize with precise file:line citations so I can go read the exact spots myself if needed.

8	 * --cpus (2 for a kind:"plugins" type, 1 for kind:"properties"/vanilla) and
9	 * --memory (>=2560m for plugins, else the configured free_minecraft_ram_mb).
10	 * Do the math: this host can run at most ONE plugin-kind server (2 of 3
11	 * vCPUs) plus one vanilla-kind server (1 vCPU) awake at once before CPU
12	 * oversubscription — RAM has more headroom, CPU is the binding constraint.
13	 *
14	 * This is deliberately NOT a queue system — just an honest "are we full"
15	 * check the paths we control (create / switch type / manual dashboard start)
16	 * can consult before starting one more container than the host can actually
17	 * run. The passive mc-router wake path (a third-party Go proxy that runs
18	 * `docker start` on its own, outside this app) is explicitly out of scope —
19	 * we don't control it and can't gate it from here.

31	 *  computation here filters to exactly this prefix so it only ever sums
32	 *  free-tier containers, never anything else that might run on this host. */
33	export const FREEMC_CONTAINER_PREFIX = "mc-free-";
34	
35	export type RunningFreemcContainer = {
36	  containerName: string;
37	  cpus: number;
38	  ramMb: number;

48	  totalRamMb: number;

147	 * stopped/nonexistent into running — never by the mc-router passive-wake
148	 * path, which this app doesn't control (see this file's module doc).

152	  addCpus: number,
153	  addRamMb: number,

158	  if (cap.committedRamMb + addRamMb > ramBudget) return { exceeds: true, dimension: "RAM" };
159	  return { exceeds: false };

736	 * given message — read-modify-write over the whole file rather than a `sed`
737	 * one-liner (unlike the IridiumSkyblock patch below) because the message
738	 * itself is full of `&` colour codes, which `sed`'s replacement syntax treats
739	 * as "insert the matched text" unless individually escaped — a real footgun
740	 * for a value built from data, not a fixed literal. Read+regex+writeback (via
741	 * execInput's stdin path, same mechanism as writeServerProperties) sidesteps
742	 * that whole class of shell/sed escaping bug entirely. Live-verified this
743	 * session: a config patched this way survives an immediate `docker restart`
744	 * (the same restart applyModeProperties always does right after this runs)
745	 * with no YAML parse errors and Essentials fully re-enabling.
746	 */
747	async function patchEssentialsJoinMessage(
748	  conn: Client,
749	  containerName: string,
750	  message: string,
751	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
752	  const path = "/data/plugins/Essentials/config.yml";
753	  const read = await dockerExec(conn, containerName, `cat ${path}`, 10_000);
754	  if (read.code !== 0) {
755	    return { ok: false, error: read.stderr.trim() || "Could not read Essentials config.yml" };
756	  }
757	  // YAML double-quoted scalar: only \ and " need escaping (our messages never
758	  // contain either today, but a future edit might).
759	  const yamlValue = message.replace(/\\/g, "\\\\").replace(/"/g, '\\"');
760	  const patched = read.stdout.replace(/^custom-join-message:.*$/m, `custom-join-message: "${yamlValue}"`);
761	  if (patched === read.stdout) {
762	    return { ok: false, error: "custom-join-message key not found in Essentials config.yml" };
763	  }
764	  const write = await execInput(
765	    conn,
766	    `docker exec -i ${shellQuote(containerName)} sh -c ${shellQuote(`cat > ${path}`)}`,
767	    patched,
768	    10_000,
769	  );
770	  if (write.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: write.stderr.trim() || "Could not write Essentials config.yml" };
771	  return { ok: true };
772	}

776	/**
777	 * Polls until the Minecraft server inside `containerName` has actually
778	 * finished booting (its log prints "Done (Ns)!") or gives up.
779	 *
780	 * This exists because BOTH of the "is it ready" checks it replaces were too
781	 * shallow: `docker inspect ...State.Running` only proves the container
782	 * PROCESS hasn't crashed — a plugin-heavy boot spends 40-90s downloading and
783	 * loading before the game itself is reachable, and that whole window used to
784	 * read as "ready". Worse, mc-router's own wake check has the identical gap:
785	 * it just opens a raw TCP connection to :25565, and Minecraft's listener
786	 * binds early, well before world/plugin loading finishes — so the port looks
787	 * "up" long before the server can actually complete a client handshake. Both
788	 * gaps together are exactly what produced a real, reproduced-live customer
789	 * bug: switching to SkyBlock reported success, mc-router's TCP check passed
790	 * within seconds, and the customer's client still got "Failed to connect —
791	 * Timed out" because the server was still mid-boot. Polling the log line
792	 * itself is the only signal that means what it says.
793	 *
794	 * `docker restart` re-runs the exact same boot sequence as a fresh `docker
795	 * run`, so this same wait is needed after `applyModeProperties`'s restart
796	 * too, not just the initial container creation.
797	 */
798	async function waitForServerReady(
799	  conn: Client,
800	  containerName: string,
801	  // 110s covers a plain/properties-only boot with room to spare. A "plugins"
802	  // preset installs its Modrinth projects (download + Paper plugin-loader
803	  // init) BEFORE the JVM's own "Done (Xs)!" timer even starts counting, which
804	  // a live, reproduced customer failure showed can push total wall-clock time
805	  // past 110s even when the JVM's own boot only reports ~76s — this function
806	  // was giving up ~2s before a real, healthy SkyBlock server finished
807	  // starting, deleting its DB row while the container kept running, orphaned
808	  // (invisible to the customer, indefinitely occupying a capacity slot).
809	  // Callers pass FREEMC_PLUGIN_READY_TIMEOUT_MS for any "plugins"-kind preset.
810	  timeoutMs = 110_000,
811	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
812	  const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
813	  // First few seconds are the container just starting up (image entrypoint,
814	  // ownership fix, etc.) — no point polling logs before that's underway.

`/etc/network/interfaces` (e.g. `auto vmbr0 ... bridge-ports ens5`). Under QEMU, a `virtio-net-pci`
device gets a PCI-Express slot-based name like `ens5` — a name that has nothing to do with the real
hardware's PCI topology. On the real physical box, the same NIC gets whatever systemd-udevd's
predictable-naming scheme actually assigns (onboard index like `eno1` takes priority when the
firmware provides `ID_NET_NAME_ONBOARD`, which `udevadm info` will show ahead of time). Since `ens5`
never exists on the real hardware, the bridge never comes up, and the OS boots completely fine with a
dead network — indistinguishable from a boot hang from the outside.

**Fix, done live via a follow-up rescue-mode session:** reboot into rescue, `apt-get install
zfs-fuse` (this rescue kernel's exact build doesn't have a matching `zfs-dkms` target — `zfs-fuse` is
a userspace ZFS impl that doesn't care) OR use Hetzner's own `/usr/local/sbin/zpool` wrapper, which
offers to compile OpenZFS from source against the *exact* running rescue kernel (works, takes ~1-2
min, answer `y` to the CDDL/GPL notice) — either way, `zpool import -N -f -R /mnt rpool`, `zfs mount`
the root + data datasets, edit `/etc/network/interfaces` to replace the QEMU-era interface name with
the real one, `zpool export rpool`, reboot. Confirmed the real interface name ahead of time via
`udevadm info -p /sys/class/net/<ifname>` while still in the FIRST rescue session (`ID_NET_NAME_ONBOARD`)
so the fix wasn't a guess.

**Lesson for next time:** decide the real interface name from `udevadm` BEFORE running the automated
install, and consider setting the answer file's network filter AND expected interface name to
whatever the real hardware will assign — or simplest, just always plan for this one manual
`/etc/network/interfaces` edit as a normal step of this onboarding method, not an exceptional failure.
Silence (no ping, no SSH) after a QEMU-installed reboot is NOT necessarily a firmware/boot-order
problem — check the installed system's actual network config from rescue mode before assuming
anything about the boot process itself. (A red herring chased first: BIOS boot-order priority hitting
a blank spare disk before the OS disks — real hardware here does default to legacy BIOS, confirmed via
`[ -d /sys/firmware/efi ]` in rescue mode, and cloning the NVMe mirror's GRUB boot code onto the blank
SATA SSD via `dd` was a reasonable, low-risk thing to try, but it was not the actual cause.)

**Template parity:** rather than building fresh cloud-init templates (9000-9004) on the new node,
`vzdump <id> --dumpdir /tank/backup` on the primary for each, `scp` the `.vma` files to the new node's
own `/tank/backup`, then `qmrestore <file> <id> --storage vmdata` — `qmrestore` preserves the
`template: 1` flag from the original config automatically (the "you can't convert a template to a
template" message on a subsequent `qm template <id>` call is expected/harmless, not an error). This
keeps every node's base images byte-identical, matching `scripts/onboard-node.sh`'s own stated
preference over `--build-templates`.

# Architectural Review: Nxeon Free Minecraft Tier — Migration Impact (VM 108 / freemc-host)

Codebase root: `/opt/nxeon`. All paths below are absolute from there unless noted.

## 0. The single most important fact

**`FreeMinecraftServer` (the Prisma model) has no foreign key to any `Server` or `Node` row at all.** Every one of the ~9 lib files that need to reach the Docker host does it by re-running the identical query:

```ts
db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" }, select: { id, rootPassword, rootPasswordEnc, sshPort, dedicatedIp: { select: { address } } } })
```

Found verbatim in:
- `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts:64-71`
- `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts:24-31`
- `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts:44-46`
- `lib/actions-freemc-mods.ts:41-43`
- `lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts:47-49`
- `lib/actions-freemc-roles.ts:128-130`
- `app/(marketing)/servers/[subdomain]/page.tsx:91-94`
- `.design-refs/check-freemc-health.ts:5` (ad-hoc ops script, same pattern)

So the **entire product is bound to one physical VM by a hardcoded string match on `Server.hostname === "freemc-host"`**, not by any ID. This is good news for migration in one sense (nothing needs a code change if the row itself is updated) and a landmine in another (a typo, a second row with that hostname, or a stale row would silently break the whole feature with no type-level protection).

---

## 1. How the app actually reaches freemc-host (the SSH control plane)

Every one of those `freemcHost()`/lookup helpers feeds into `withServerSsh()` (`lib/ssh-exec.ts`), which delegates connection-target resolution to **`lib/sftp.ts:137-143`**:

```ts
export function connectionTarget(server: SftpServer) {
  const dedicated = !!server.dedicatedIp;
  const host = dedicated ? server.dedicatedIp!.address : process.env.PUBLIC_IP || "";
  const port = dedicated ? 22 : server.sshPort;
  ...
}
```

This is the **only** logic that decides where Docker/RCON commands over SSH actually go. Two mutually exclusive cases:

- **Case A — `freemc-host` has a `DedicatedIp` row** (`prisma/schema.prisma:1075-1095`, one-to-one via `DedicatedIp.serverId`): SSH goes straight to `dedicatedIp.address:22`. That `DedicatedIp` row itself belongs to a specific `nodeId` (`DedicatedIp.nodeId → Node`, schema:1087-1088) and has an `ovhBlock` field that is **OVH-specific** and explicitly documented as unused for Hetzner rows (schema:1078: `"unused (kept "") for Hetzner rows"`).
- **Case B — no dedicated IP (NAT/port-forward model)**: SSH goes to `process.env.PUBLIC_IP:server.sshPort` — a single **global environment variable**, not scoped per node, not derived from `Server.nodeId`/`Node.publicIp` at all in this code path (contrast with `worker/index.ts:712/814` and `app/admin/servers/page.tsx:133`, which *do* prefer `server.node?.publicIp` first — `lib/sftp.ts`'s `connectionTarget` is inconsistent with those and never consults the Node relation).

**I cannot tell you from static code which case applies to the live `freemc-host` row** — that's a live-DB fact — but the wording of the admin setting is a strong signal toward Case B: `lib/actions-settings.ts:258` calls `free_minecraft_public_ip` *"the public IP the wildcard DNS record and NAT/DNAT rule should point at"*. A NAT/DNAT rule is only meaningful for a NAT (non-dedicated-IP) guest. **Verify this before migrating**: check whether `DedicatedIp.serverId` points at the `freemc-host` Server row.

### Why this matters enormously for the OVH→Hetzner move
If Case B applies, SSH control of freemc-host depends on `process.env.PUBLIC_IP` (currently presumably `51.79.162.96`) plus a NAT/DNAT rule forwarding `sshPort` to freemc-host's internal `10.20.x.x` address — **and that DNAT rule is only ever created/maintained on the machine where the Nxeon worker process itself physically runs**, via `worker/network.ts`. This is a **documented, unfixed platform bug**, not my speculation:

- `worker/network.ts:16`: `const CHAIN = process.env.NXEON_NAT_CHAIN ?? "NXEON_FWD"` — one hardcoded chain name, one global env var, no per-node variant.
- `worker/network.ts:89-96` (`syncPortForwards`): `db.server.findMany({ where: { ipAddress: {not:null}, sshPort: {not:null}, status: {notIn:[...]} } })` — **no `nodeId` filter whatsoever**. Every NAT-eligible server platform-wide is folded into one `intent` and reconciled against **one local iptables chain** via `iptablesHost()` (plain `execFile("iptables", ...)`, not SSH to a remote node).
- `scripts/onboard-node.sh:111-113,181`: names the *intended* per-node chain `NXEON_FWD_N${NODE_NUM}` for a second node, but explicitly comments `"we do NOT create/populate it here — the worker owns the NXEON_FWD* DNAT chain"` — and the worker, per the point above, never populates anything but the single primary chain.
- This exact failure mode is written up as **`docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md` P1-18** (`worker/network.ts:7`, `lib/actions-nodes.ts:21,128-131,174-200`, `app/admin/nodes/new/page.tsx:24-25`): *"admin registers node-2 via `/admin/nodes/new`... The worker flushes `NXEON_FWD` on the primary host and adds a DNAT to an address that host cannot route. `NXEON_FWD_N2` is never created on node-2. Every node-2 VM has dead SSH while `/admin/nodes` shows the node green/ONLINE."*

**Bottom line: if freemc-host is a NAT-style (non-dedicated-IP) server today, moving it to the Hetzner node as currently onboarded will very likely leave it with dead SSH from the app's perspective, exactly as P1-18 predicts**, unless you either (a) manually build the equivalent DNAT rule on the Hetzner box yourself, working around the worker, or (b) give freemc-host a real dedicated/floating IP on Hetzner instead and set `DedicatedIp.address` + `nodeId` accordingly, which sidesteps this whole class of bug (Case A path is direct, no NAT chain involved).

---

## 2. `docs/MIGRATION.md` — the platform's own migration runbook

This is the authoritative internal doc for exactly this kind of move (105 lines, read in full). Key points directly applicable:

- **Strategy A ("Graceful, VM-by-VM")** is the documented playbook for moving one VM to a second node without downtime to everything else — matches your scenario precisely.
- Its own instructions (line 43-44): *"Update that server's `nodeId`, `ipAddress`, `sshPort`, `node.publicIp` in the DB and re-run the port-forward sync."* — i.e., the runbook itself assumes the port-forward sync (`worker/network.ts`) actually works per-node, which per P1-18 it does **not**. The runbook and the code are out of sync; be aware you may be the first real exercise of this gap.
- Line 52-53 caveat: *"VMs on different physical boxes are separate NAT islands (no cross-host private networking without a WireGuard/VXLAN overlay)"* — freemc-host's Docker network (`--network freemc`, `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts:918`) is entirely self-contained on the guest itself, so this doesn't affect internal container networking, only the app→host SSH path and player→host game-port path discussed above.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md:7237-7238` confirms the Hetzner node (**"node-2", auction server #3068915, Falkenstein, `nxeon-fsn1`, 178.63.94.114**) was *already onboarded* (today, 2026-09-05) via the QEMU rescue-mode Proxmox install method. Whether a matching `Node` row was actually created in `/admin/nodes/new` afterward is a DB fact I can't confirm from code — check the `Node` table for a row with `provider = HETZNER`, `region = "fsn1"`, `publicIp = "178.63.94.114"`.

---

## 3. Per-file breakdown

### `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts` (645 lines) — customer-facing actions
- `freemcHost()` (61-71): the hostname lookup described above.
- `createFreeMinecraftServer` (78-225): checks `free_minecraft_enabled`, live capacity via SSH, creates the DB row, then SSHes in to `mkdir` a data dir at `/opt/freemc/servers/<row.id>` and calls `recreateGameTypeContainer`. Rollback path `docker rm -f` on failure. No node/IP assumptions beyond the SSH host resolution already covered.
- `deleteFreeMinecraftServer` (227-245), `powerAction`/start/stop/restart (269-341), `renameFreeMinecraftServer` (343-355, cosmetic only), `changeFreeMinecraftSubdomain` (357-441, stop→remove→recreate with new `mc-router.host` label), `sendFreeMinecraftCommand` (443-463, RCON), settings get/apply (478-540), legacy preset apply (542-645) — all route every remote op through the same `freemcHost()` → `withServerSsh()` chain. No other hardcoded IP/host in this file.
- Settings read here: `free_minecraft_enabled`, `free_minecraft_max_concurrent`, `free_minecraft_domain` (default `"play.nxeon.cloud"`), `free_minecraft_ram_mb`.

### `lib/actions-admin-freemc.ts` (202 lines) — admin actions
- Identical `freemcHost()` helper (24-31), independently duplicated (module doc at line 4-11 explicitly notes this is a deliberate separate surface from the customer actions).
- `adminGetFreeMinecraftStatus`, `adminUnpublishFreeMinecraftServer`, `adminDeleteFreeMinecraftServer`, `adminGetFreemcHostCapacity` — all gated by `requireArea("fleet")`, all resolve the host the same way, no other node/IP logic.

### `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts`, `-worlds.ts`, `-mods.ts`, `-roles.ts`, `-public.ts`
All follow the exact same `hostname: "freemc-host"` lookup + `withServerSsh` pattern (confirmed by grep, see citations in §0). `-public.ts` is the one exception — it's pure DB (opt-in public directory listing toggle), never touches SSH/container/host at all (its own doc comment says so explicitly, lines 6-9). None of these introduce any additional IP/node dependency beyond what's already covered.

### `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` (1061 lines) — the Docker/RCON primitives
- No DB/host lookups itself — it's a "plain module" that receives an already-open `Client` (ssh2 connection) from callers. No node/IP assumptions.
- `recreateGameTypeContainer` (851-1061) is where the actual `docker run` command is assembled (915-928): `--network freemc`, `--label mc-router.host=<subdomain>.<domain>`, `-e EULA=TRUE -e TYPE=... -e ONLINE_MODE=FALSE -e MEMORY=...`, etc. **The `--network freemc` Docker network and the `mc-router` container itself are NOT created/managed by any code in this repo** — they must already exist on the host as a one-time manual setup step (confirmed by `.design-refs/check-freemc-health.ts:13`, which just inspects a running `mc-router` container by name — nothing provisions it).
- **mc-router config generation, answered directly**: there is no config file generation at all. `itzg/mc-router` (a third-party Go proxy) auto-discovers routes via **Docker labels** (`mc-router.host=<subdomain>.<domain>`, line 920) using its own Docker-socket-watch mode. The platform never writes a router config file, never calls a router API — it purely sets a label on `docker run`/recreate and mc-router does the rest, including the auto-sleep/wake-on-connect and idle-stop behavior (module doc, lines 269-274 in `-worlds.ts`/`freemc-capacity.ts`). **This means after migration, `mc-router` itself must be running on whichever box hosts the containers** — it is part of what has to physically move with the VM (it's inside the VM, not a separate piece of Nxeon infra, so a VM-level vzdump/qmrestore or full-disk copy carries it along fine).
- `FREEMC_RESERVED_CPUS`/`FREEMC_RESERVED_RAM_MB` and the whole `freemc-capacity.ts` accounting (see below) are based on **live** `nproc`/`free -m` queries against the host every time — i.e. genuinely dynamic, not hardcoded to freemc-host's current OVH hardware specs. If Hetzner's box has different CPU/RAM, this self-adjusts automatically; no code change needed. The extensive module comments (lines 6-12, freemc-capacity.ts) do document *today's* OVH numbers (7.8GB RAM / 3 vCPU) purely as historical/audit context — those are comments, not enforced constants.

### `lib/freemc-capacity.ts` (160 lines)
Fully covered above. `FREEMC_CONTAINER_PREFIX = "mc-free-"` (line 33) — a naming convention, not host-specific. All capacity math queries the host live via SSH each call — no hardcoded host facts baked in beyond the reserved-margin constants (`FREEMC_RESERVED_CPUS=1`, `FREEMC_RESERVED_RAM_MB=1024`), which are safety margins, not IP/host identifiers.

### `lib/game-subdomain-dns.ts` (108 lines)
Its own module doc (lines 4-25) is explicit that this file is for **PAID** Minecraft subdomains only (`Server.subdomain`, per-server exact-name A+SRV records against Cloudflare, using platform token `CLOUDFLARE_DNS_API_TOKEN`). It reuses `gameSubdomainBase()` (line 40-42) which reads the *same* `free_minecraft_domain` setting the free tier uses, since paid and free share one base zone (`play.nxeon.cloud`) — free servers get covered by one shared wildcard record, paid servers get their own exact-name record that takes DNS precedence. **This file does not touch the free-tier wildcard record at all** — nothing in the repo does (see next point).

### The free-tier wildcard DNS record — not automated anywhere
Extensive search (`play.nxeon.cloud`, `wildcard`) turned up no code that creates or updates the `*.<free_minecraft_domain>` A record. It is a **manually-managed, one-time Cloudflare DNS record**, pointed at whatever IP is currently in the `free_minecraft_public_ip` setting — the setting's own comment says as much: *"Set once after provisioning; not auto-synced from the Server row"* (`lib/actions-settings.ts:260`). **This is a required manual step on migration**: after freemc-host's public IP changes, someone must manually update this Cloudflare A record (and the setting) — nothing in the app will do it automatically, and nothing will warn you if it's stale (players would just get connection timeouts on the new IP while the old one still resolves).

### `lib/actions-settings.ts` — `free_minecraft` settings block (lines 253-280)
| Setting | Type | Purpose | Migration relevance |
|---|---|---|---|
| `free_minecraft_enabled` | bool | master feature flag | none |
| `free_minecraft_public_ip` | string | *"public IP the wildcard DNS record and NAT/DNAT rule should point at"* — explicitly **not auto-synced** from the `Server` row | **must be manually updated to `178.63.94.114`** (or whatever new IP/port-forward target is used) as part of migration |
| `free_minecraft_domain` | string | wildcard base domain, default `play.nxeon.cloud` | unaffected by node migration |
| `free_minecraft_ram_mb` | int | per-container Docker `--memory` cap | unaffected |
| `free_minecraft_disk_mb` | int | documented as **not yet enforced anywhere** (module doc, `actions-free-minecraft.ts:9-13`) | unaffected |
| `free_minecraft_idle_minutes` | int | mc-router's `-auto-scale-down-after` value — **note**: nothing in this repo actually passes this value to the mc-router container's own startup flags; verify mc-router's actual runtime flags on the host match this setting, since it appears to be read only for display/admin-panel purposes | worth double-checking post-migration that mc-router on the new box was started with matching flags |
| `free_minecraft_max_concurrent` | int | global cap on concurrently-awake free servers | unaffected |

### Prisma models
- `FreeMinecraftServer` (`prisma/schema.prisma:2600-2666`) and `FreeMinecraftWorld` (2670-2687): **no relation to `Server` or `Node` at all** — confirmed, see §0. The architecture note atop the model (2600-2609) is explicit: *"NOT a Server row itself (this isn't a Proxmox VM)."*
- `Server` model (552-720ish): has `nodeId String? / node Node?` (the actual FK, used by ordinary Proxmox-provisioned VPS servers) and a one-to-one reverse `dedicatedIp DedicatedIp?` relation (line 721). The `freemc-host` row is *a* `Server` row, so it *can* carry a `nodeId` and a `dedicatedIp`, exactly like any customer VPS — but nothing in the free-tier code path ever reads `Server.nodeId` for anything (see §1's Case A/B split — SSH resolution in `lib/sftp.ts` ignores the Node relation entirely).
- `Node` model (1151-1190): `publicIp`, `apiUrl`/`tokenId`/`tokenSecret` (Proxmox API creds), `provider` (`OVH`/`HETZNER`), `region`, `isPrimary`, `natChain`, `subnetPrefix`, etc. **This is the row that will need a Hetzner entry** (per `docs/MIGRATION.md` Strategy A step 2) if it doesn't already exist, and freemc-host's `Server.nodeId` should point to it after the move — primarily so the **generic** admin server-management surface (`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx:42-48`) resolves the right Proxmox API (`pveForNode(server.node)`) for power actions/console/live-status on VM 108. If `nodeId` is left stale (still OVH) after the VM physically moves, admin Start/Stop/Reboot/Console for VM 108 will silently target the **wrong Proxmox host** — either erroring, or worse, acting on VMID 108 if the old node still has a stale leftover VM with that ID.
- `DedicatedIp` model (1075-1095): as discussed, this is the deciding factor for whether SSH uses a real dedicated IP or falls back to global `PUBLIC_IP`.

---

## 4. Admin & customer UI surfaces

- `app/admin/free-minecraft/page.tsx` — fleet-wide list of every `FreeMinecraftServer` row; deliberately does **not** batch-fetch live status (perf reasons, lines 58-67), uses on-demand per-row SSH via `components/admin/FreeMinecraftControls.tsx`'s `CheckStatusButton`. No IP/node hardcoding beyond the same `hostname:"freemc-host"` pattern via `adminGetFreeMinecraftStatus`.
- `components/admin/settings/FreeMinecraftPanel.tsx` — the settings form UI; renders the `free_minecraft_public_ip` field with hint text explicitly calling out *"what the wildcard DNS record and the port-forward rule point at"* (line 30) — this is the one place an operator manually types in the new IP after migration.
- `components/admin/FreeMinecraftControls.tsx` — capacity panel + per-server admin buttons (check status, unpublish, delete). No host-specific hardcoding beyond cosmetic strings ("freemc-host capacity" heading, line 117; delete-confirmation copy, line 242).
- `app/(marketing)/servers/[subdomain]/page.tsx` and `app/(marketing)/servers/page.tsx` — the public server directory; both do the same best-effort, timeout-bounded live-status SSH lookup (lines 79-103 in `[subdomain]/page.tsx`), gracefully degrading to "status unknown" on any failure (including host unreachable) — this is a nice safety property: **a botched migration would make status show as unknown/offline on marketing pages rather than crash them**.
- `app/dashboard/free-minecraft/page.tsx` and `components/customer/freemc/FreeMcDashboard.tsx` / `SavedWorldsPanel.tsx` — the customer dashboard; no host/IP hardcoding found, same SSH round-trip pattern, deliberately avoided on page load per `app/dashboard/games/page.tsx:18` comment.
- `app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx` — the **generic** (non-freemc-specific) server detail/power-control page. Relevant because `freemc-host` IS a normal `Server` row and would show up here too if an admin navigates to it directly. This page's live VM status/power path is fully `Server.nodeId`-dependent (`pveForNode(server.node)`, line 48) — again, the piece that needs `nodeId` updated post-migration.

## 5. Every hardcoded primary-node-IP / VMID-108 reference found platform-wide

Grepped for `51.79.162.96`, `178.63.94.114`, `freemc-host`, VMID literal `108`. None of the freemc-specific files hardcode an IP or VMID — they all resolve host identity dynamically via the DB (weak point: by hostname string, not ID, as noted in §0). The hardcoded-IP hits found are **outside** the free-Minecraft feature but worth flagging since they touch the same primary-node identity your migration reasoning depends on:

| File:line | What it is |
|---|---|
| `lib/dedicated-ip.ts:84` | `ovhGateway()` back-compat wrapper: `ovhGatewayFor(process.env.PUBLIC_IP ?? "51.79.162.96")` — hardcoded fallback literal |
| `prisma/seed.ts:153` | Dev/seed script prints `process.env.APP_URL ?? "http://51.79.162.96/"` in a generated admin-credentials file — dev tooling only |
| `scripts/set-mail-ptr.ts:3` | `const IP = "51.79.162.96"` — unrelated mail PTR-record helper script |
| `components/marketing/HeroVisual.tsx:61`, `components/marketing/DeployCard.tsx:18`, `components/admin/EmailTemplateEditor.tsx:54`, `app/admin/email-templates/page.tsx:114-115` | Marketing copy / example SSH command strings for illustration only — cosmetic, not functional |
| `scripts/firewall-safe-apply.sh`, `scripts/firewall.nft`, `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` (many) | Firewall/ops runbook references to the current OVH box's IP — infra-side, not app-code, but confirms `51.79.162.96` is indeed treated platform-wide as *the* primary node's identity in scripts/docs, reinforcing that `PUBLIC_IP` is effectively "the OVH box" today |

None of these sit on the freemc execution path, but they confirm `process.env.PUBLIC_IP` (and its literal `51.79.162.96` fallback) is deeply assumed, platform-wide, to mean "the one box everything NAT-based runs behind" — exactly the assumption that breaks for any NAT-style server on a second node (§1).

**No literal `108` (VMID) appears anywhere in application code** — VMID is only ever looked up dynamically via `Server.vmid` from the DB, so there's no code-level reference to update for that specific number.

---

## 6. Direct answer to "is there a Node/nodeId relationship for this VM?"

**Yes, structurally** — `freemc-host` is a normal `Server` row and the `Server` model has `nodeId → Node`. **But functionally, no part of the free-Minecraft feature ever reads it.** The feature's entire runtime behavior (SSH target, capacity math, DNS target) is driven by:
1. A string match on `Server.hostname === "freemc-host"` (to find *which* Server row), then
2. `Server.dedicatedIp` XOR global `process.env.PUBLIC_IP` + `Server.sshPort` (to find *where* to connect), completely bypassing `Server.nodeId`/`Node.publicIp`.

The only place `Server.nodeId` would matter for this specific VM is the **generic** admin fleet UI (`app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx`) for Proxmox-level power/console actions, and any capacity/IP-pool logic in `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`/`lib/capacity.ts` if freemc-host ever falls into those paths (e.g., IP-pool assignment, which does branch by `Node.provider` for OVH vs. Hetzner API calls).

---

## 7. Migration checklist implied by this review

1. Confirm (via DB, not code) whether `freemc-host`'s `Server` row currently has a `DedicatedIp` (Case A) or relies on NAT/`PUBLIC_IP` (Case B) — this determines everything else.
2. Confirm/create the Hetzner `Node` row (`provider=HETZNER`, `publicIp=178.63.94.114`, `region=fsn1`) if not already present from the 2026-09-05 onboarding.
3. Move the VM (vzdump/qmrestore or equivalent) per `docs/MIGRATION.md` Strategy A — this carries `mc-router`, the `freemc` Docker network, and all `mc-free-*` containers/data along automatically since they live inside the guest.
4. Update the `freemc-host` `Server` row: `nodeId` → new Node, `ipAddress`/`sshPort` as applicable, and either attach a new `DedicatedIp` row (if going the dedicated-IP route) or ensure NAT port-forwarding is genuinely working on the Hetzner box.
5. **If Case B (NAT)**: do NOT trust the automatic port-forward sync — per documented bug P1-18, `worker/network.ts` cannot manage a second node's iptables. Either fix that worker (scope `syncPortForwards`/`CHAIN` per node, actually use `Node.natChain`), or manually build the equivalent DNAT rule on the Hetzner box and manually keep `process.env.PUBLIC_IP` semantics in mind (it's a single global value platform-wide — changing it to fix freemc-host would misroute every other NAT server too, so don't just flip `PUBLIC_IP`).
6. Manually update the `free_minecraft_public_ip` setting (Admin → Settings → Free Minecraft panel) to the new player-facing IP.
7. Manually update the Cloudflare wildcard A record for `*.play.nxeon.cloud` to the new IP (no code does this automatically).
8. Verify mc-router inside the guest was started/is running with flags consistent with `free_minecraft_idle_minutes`.
9. Spot-check `app/admin/servers/[id]/page.tsx` for VM 108 to confirm Proxmox power/console actions resolve to the new node correctly (validates step 4's `nodeId` update).
10. Re-run a live capacity check (`adminGetFreemcHostCapacity` / the admin Free Minecraft page's capacity panel) — this is fully dynamic (`nproc`/`free -m`) so it will just work once SSH connectivity is restored, no code changes needed for differing Hetzner hardware specs.
